title: Controlled Preemption: Amplifying Side-Channel Attacks from Userspace
problem: Many microarchitectural side-channel attacks are hampered by low temporal resolution measurements, which can preclude or significantly complicate extraction of sensitive information. Userspace attackers lack a mechanism to synchronize their observations with victim activity at fine-grained time resolution.
motivation: Microarchitectural side channels remain a persistent threat in modern systems, but the effectiveness of many attack methodologies is fundamentally limited by coarse measurement granularity caused by unpredictable OS scheduling.
method: The paper introduces controlled preemption, a technique that allows a userspace attacker to precisely manipulate OS preemption timing in order to achieve fine-grained, synchronized measurement of victim microarchitectural state. By forcing preemption at attacker-chosen moments, the technique amplifies the signal quality of side-channel observations without requiring privileged access or hardware modifications.
key_novelty: Userspace-accessible controlled preemption mechanism that amplifies microarchitectural side-channel attacks by enabling precise attacker-controlled timing of OS preemption events.
contributions: Controlled preemption technique enabling userspace attackers to synchronize side-channel measurements with victim execution at fine granularity
Demonstration that low-temporal-resolution side-channel attacks can be significantly amplified using this technique
Analysis of the security implications of OS scheduling mechanisms exploitable from userspace
